Let $\Cd$ be the category of non-empty finite linearly ordered $3$-uniform hypergraphs in which every non-empty set $U$ of vertices satisfies $2|U|-3e(U)>0$, where $e(U)$ is the number of hyperedges contained in $U$, with the closed embeddings as arrows \textup{(}Definition~\ref{def:cdelta}\textup{)}. Then $\Cd$ is total, and for every non-zero ring $R$ the colimit functor on $\Cd$-indexed diagrams of $R$-modules is not exact.
The category $\mathcal T$ of finite ordered two-graphs and their embeddings is quasi-filtered and is not total.

Among non-empty connected small categories, \[ \{\text{filtered}\}\subsetneq\{\text{exact}\}\subsetneq\{\text{total}\} \subsetneq\{\text{quasi-filtered}\}. \] The three inclusions are strict by the category $\Delta_{\mathrm{inj}}$ of the finite non-empty ordinals and increasing injections, by $\Cd$, and by $\mathcal T$. Moreover a non-empty connected category is filtered if and only if it is total and sifted.
Let $A$ be a category all of whose action components have the integral homology of a point. Then all action components of $A$ are weakly contractible.
A non-empty connected category $A$ is total if and only if every action component of $A$ is weakly contractible.
Let $A$ be a non-empty connected category. If $A$ is filtered it is exact, and if $A$ is exact it is total.
Let $D$ be a connected category such that $H_1(B\El(K);\Z)=0$ for every functor $K\colon D\to\Set$ with $\El(K)$ connected. Then any two objects of $D$ have a common successor.
Let $A$ be a non-empty connected category such that $H_1(BD;\Z)=0$ for every action component $D$ of $A$. Then $A$ is quasi-filtered. In particular every total category is quasi-filtered.
A non-empty connected category is filtered if and only if it is total and sifted.
In a category with \textup{(SC)} every pair of arrows $f\colon a\to b$, $f'\colon a\to b'$ can be completed to a commutative square $uf=u'f'$.

Assume \textup{(K1)--(K4)}, and let $L\colon\mathcal A\to\Set$ be a functor. For every connected component $D$ of $\El(L)$, either $D$ is weakly contractible, or the projection $D\to\mathcal A$ is a weak equivalence.

Let $D$ and $E$ be finite linearly ordered sets, $B,C\subseteq D$, $F=B\cap C$, and let $d_0,d_1\colon D\to E$ be increasing injections that agree on $F$. For every sufficiently large integer $N\ge 2$, with $s=2N$, there are a finite linearly ordered set $Z$, an increasing injection $e\colon E\to Z$ and increasing injections $a_0,\dots,a_s\colon D\to Z$ with the following properties. Put $Z_0=e(E)$ and $Z_i=a_i(D)$ for $0<i<s$; these are the \emph{pieces}, and their indices are read modulo $s$. \begin{enumerate} \item[\textup{(i)}] $Z=\bigcup_iZ_i$; $a_0=ed_0$ and $a_s=ed_1$; $a_{2j}|_B=a_{2j+1}|_B$ and $a_{2j+1}|_C=a_{2j+2}|_C$ for $0\le j<N$. \item[\textup{(ii)}] For $x\in F$ the point $a_i(x)$ does not depend on $i$; these \emph{$F$-points} lie in every piece. Every other point of $Z$ lies in at most three pieces. If it lies in two pieces, these are consecutive, or they are $Z_1$ and $Z_{s-1}$, and then the point lies in $Z_0$ as well. \item[\textup{(iii)}] For $0\le i<s$ we have $Z_i\cap Z_{i+1}=a_i(B)=a_{i+1}(B)$ if $i$ is even and $Z_i\cap Z_{i+1}=a_i(C)=a_{i+1}(C)$ if $i$ is odd. \item[\textup{(iv)}] For every index $r$ there are a finite set $L$, a surjection $q\colon L\to Z$ and subsets $T_0,\dots,T_{s-1}$ covering $L$ such that $q$ maps $T_k$ bijectively onto $Z_{r+k}$, with these properties: every point of $L$ lies in $T_k$ for a set of consecutive values of $k$, with at most three elements unless the point lies over an $F$-point; $q(T_{k-1}\cap T_k)=Z_{r+k-1}\cap Z_{r+k}$ for $0<k<s$; every $F$-point has one preimage under $q$; and $q$ is injective except that at most $\max(|B|,|C|)$ points of $Z$ have two preimages. \end{enumerate}

closure calculus: Let $X$ be a hypergraph. \begin{enumerate} \item[\textup{(a)}] $\delta(U)+\delta(U')\ge\delta(U\cup U')+\delta(U\cap U')$ for all $U,U'\subseteq X$. \item[\textup{(b)}] If $A\cle B$ and $Y\subseteq B$, then $A\cap Y\cle Y$. \item[\textup{(c)}] If $A\cle B$ and $B\cle C$, then $A\cle C$. \item[\textup{(d)}] Let $X=B\cup C$ and $A=B\cap C$, and suppose that $E_X=E_X(B)\cup E_X(C)$ \textup{(}we then call $X$ the \emph{free amalgam} of $B$ and $C$ over $A$\textup{)}. Then for every $U\subseteq X$ \begin{equation} \delta(U)=\delta(U\cap B)+\delta(U\cap C)-\delta(U\cap A). \end{equation} If moreover $B$ and $C$ are positive, $A\cle B$ and $A\cle C$, then $X$ is positive, $B\cle X$ and $C\cle X$. Here $A$ may be empty. \end{enumerate}

There is a countable ordered hypergraph $M$, all of whose finite subsets are positive, with the following properties. \begin{enumerate} \item[\textup{(M1)}] Every finite subset of $M$ is contained in a finite subset $B$ with $B\cle M$. \item[\textup{(M2)}] If $B\cle M$ is finite and $f\colon B\to C$ is a closed embedding into a finite positive ordered hypergraph, there is an embedding $h\colon C\to M$ with $h(C)\cle M$ and $hf=\id_B$. \item[\textup{(M3)}] Every isomorphism between two finite closed subsets of $M$ extends to an automorphism of $M$. \end{enumerate}
The triple $(M,G,\K)$ satisfies \textup{(K1)}. For $B,C\in\K$ the arrows $B\to C$ of $\mathcal A$ are exactly the closed embeddings $B\to C$, and $\mathcal A$ is equivalent to $\Cd$.
$(M,G,\K)$ satisfies \textup{(K2)}: $\Fix_M(G_B)=B$ for every $B\in\K$.
The category $\mathcal A$ satisfies \textup{(SC)}, and $B\mathcal A$ is weakly contractible.

the bridge: Let $D$ and $E$ be positive ordered hypergraphs, let $B\cle D$ and $C\cle D$, put $F=B\cap C$, and let $d_0,d_1\colon D\to E$ be closed embeddings that agree on $F$. Then there are a positive ordered hypergraph $Z$, a closed embedding $e\colon E\to Z$ and closed embeddings $a_0,\dots,a_{2N}\colon D\to Z$ with \[ a_0=ed_0,\quad a_{2N}=ed_1,\quad a_{2j}|_B=a_{2j+1}|_B,\quad a_{2j+1}|_C=a_{2j+2}|_C\qquad(0\le j<N). \]
For all $B,C\in\K$ we have $\langle G_B,G_C\rangle=G_{B\cap C}$.
$(M,G,\K)$ satisfies \textup{(K3)}: every open subgroup of $G$ is $G_F$ for some $F\in\K$.
The category $\Cd$ is total: it is non-empty and connected, and for every functor $L\colon\Cd\to\Set$ every connected component of $\El(L)$ is weakly contractible.

Let $R$ be a non-zero ring. For an object $X$ of $\Cd$ let $P_X=R[\Cd(X,-)]$, a functor from $\Cd$ to left $R$-modules, and let \[ \Theta\colon P_W\longrightarrow P_V\oplus P_V,\qquad \Theta(g)=(gv_2-gv_1,\ gv_3-gv_1)\quad(g\colon W\to X). \] Then $\Theta$ is a monomorphism, and $\colim\Theta\colon R\to R\oplus R$ is zero. In particular the functor $\colim$ from $\Cd$-indexed diagrams of $R$-modules to $R$-modules is not exact; for $R=\Z$, the category $\Cd$ is not exact.

anchored amalgams: Let $S=S_1\cup S_2$ and let $c_i$ be a two-graph on $S_i$, $i=1,2$, such that $c_1$ and $c_2$ agree on the triples contained in $S_1\cap S_2$. Choose $p_i\in S_i$, with $p_1=p_2\in S_1\cap S_2$ if this set is non-empty, and let $b$ be the graph on $S$ that equals $(c_i)_{p_i}$ on the pairs contained in $S_i$ and is zero on all other pairs. Then $\partial b$ is a two-graph on $S$ that restricts to $c_i$ on $S_i$.

There is an ordered two-graph structure on a countably infinite set $M$ \textup{(}a linear order and a function $c$ on three-element subsets that is a two-graph on every finite subset\textup{)} such that: \begin{enumerate} \item[\textup{(N2)}] if $Y\subseteq M$ is finite and $f\colon Y\to C$ is an embedding into an ordered two-graph, there is an embedding $h\colon C\to M$ with $hf=\id_Y$ \textup{(}here $Y$ may be empty\textup{)}; \item[\textup{(N3)}] every isomorphism between finite subsets of $M$ extends to an automorphism of $M$. \end{enumerate}
$(M,G,\K)$ satisfies \textup{(K2)} and \textup{(K4)}.
Let $B,C\subseteq M$ be finite with $B\cap C\ne\varnothing$. Then $\langle G_B,G_C\rangle=G_{B\cap C}$.
For distinct points $x,y$ of $M$ we have $\langle G_{\{x\}},G_{\{y\}}\rangle=G$.
For all finite $B,C\subseteq M$ we have $\langle G_B,G_C\rangle=G_{B\cap C}$, and $(M,G,\K)$ satisfies \textup{(K3)}.
$B\mathcal T$ is simply connected.
$H_2(B\mathcal T;\F_2)\ne 0$.
Every action component of $\mathcal T$ is weakly contractible or weakly equivalent to $\mathcal T$. Consequently $\mathcal T$ is quasi-filtered, and it is not total.
